summary: The stated behaviour occurs, but at the commits the ledger records as fixes, not at the affected one; the commit roles appear inverted. With any_precision not installed: at 162f99ab8bb0 (listed latest affected) importing eval/compare_q_anyprecision.py raised ModuleNotFoundError "No module named 'any_precision'" at line 2, so the import problem was reported up front. At db65151b07e7 and 1f7f3e94c0e6 (listed fixes) and at 6171f9af3d4b between them, the import was swallowed by the new try/except guard and load_anyprecision raised NameError "name 'AnyPrecisionForCausalLM' is not defined" (line 85 / 87), without reporting the original import failure. That is the defect as described, but introduced by db65151b07e7 and widened by 1f7f3e94c0e6 (which also catches ImportError). A reviewer should decide how the ledger records introduction and fix.
what_ran: repro.py imports the worktree's eval/compare_q_anyprecision.py unmodified and calls load_anyprecision on the Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct directory (what compare_q.py dispatches to for load_fn 'anyprecision'), in py312-compareq-torch26cu126 where any_precision is not installed. No GPU needed.
limits: Only the first-import-failure case (package absent). The second-import case (first import succeeds, AnyPrecisionLinear fails, NameError in get_storage_info) needs a partially working any_precision install and was not exercised. compare_q.py's own dispatch and dataset setup were not run; load_anyprecision was called directly.
